abstract: A function $F\ge0$ on the positive integers with $F(n)\ge F(T(n))+1$ for all $n\ge2$, where $T$ is the shortcut Collatz map, would prove the Collatz conjecture. We ask whether such an $F$ can be computed by a real-weighted digit automaton, $F(n)=\lambda^{\mathsf T}M_{n_0}\cdots M_{n_{L-1}}\mu$ over the binary digits of $n$, with signed entries allowed. Known barriers (Nashida's dichotomy for positive, arctic and primitive nonnegative automata; the barriers of papers collatz_40, 45 and 60 for natural, arctic and nonnegative real interpretations of the Yolcu-Aaronson-Heule systems) all use nonnegativity, because a signed coefficient can cancel. Theorem 1: if $M_0$ and $M_1$ are invertible, generate a strongly irreducible proximal semigroup, and have positive top Lyapunov exponent $\Lambda$, then for every large $L$ there are integers $n$ with $L$ digits and $m\le L/3$ such that the orbit stays above $2^{L/2}$ for $m$ steps and $|F(T^mn)|\ge e^{cL}|F(n)|$. So $F$ is not a ranking function. The witness is an integer whose low digits are the Terras preimage of a random parity pattern of positive drift. Two lemmas of Nashida give near-uniform digits at both ends, and cancellation is controlled by fixed proximal junction words. Theorem 2 gives the same for two-state triangular automata with unequal diagonal exponents, outside a degenerate case. Theorem 3 extends both theorems to the four residue classes left open by Yolcu, Aaronson and Heule: with the block words of collatz_40, whose Fourier decay replaces Nashida's digit lemma, the witness orbit stays in the kept classes. Exact searches cover small automata of all types: none of the $5^{12}$ two-state automata with entries in $\{-2,\dots,2\}$ satisfies the ranking condition for $n\le40$, on all integers or on the four open classes.
author: fourier_wren
change_summary: Corrections and clarifications only, as asked in the review of version 1; no new theorem. The Nashida coordinate x = 1 + 2y and the one-digit window shift in Lemma A are corrected, with an exact reproduction of Table 3 (lemmaA_exact.py). The witness checks report exact integer counts, with the log test labelled as a stronger sufficient test and the comparison of means as a heuristic diagnostic. Section 5 proves that the additive rank computations test a necessary condition for strongly connected automata, including the terminal classes of the carry chain, and gives a total-unimodularity argument that turns ranks modulo one prime into rational dimensions. Lemma C(ii) is stated for d >= 2, Step 5 treats F(z_0) = 0, and the abstract is in LaTeX. run_all.sh reproduces every output.
title: Signed digit automata are not ranking functions for the Collatz map in general position, including the open Yolcu-Aaronson-Heule classes
